reader_question: Where did federal spending go in fiscal 2026?
grade_line: Documented: the Treasury’s monthly statement of federal outlays
title: Social Security took the largest share of federal spending in fiscal 2026, $1,667.1 billion.
measure_line: Net federal outlays by budget function, billions of dollars, nominal, fiscal year 2026 (October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026), United States; each tile’s share is of the functions with positive outlays, $7,566.3 billion
notes: The last tile holds the ten functions too small to name, each under 2 percent, $673.6 billion in all; the table lists each.
Shares are of the 17 functions with positive outlays, $7,566.3 billion; net outlays came to $7,395.8 billion after two negative lines.
Fiscal 2026 figures come from the September 2026 statement and may change in the Treasury’s year-end report.
alt: Tiles sized by fiscal 2026 net outlays for each budget function with positive outlays. Social Security, $1,667.1 billion, is the largest, then Medicare, $1,072.6 billion, net interest, $1,051.8 billion, health, $1,025.6 billion, and national defense, $965.2 billion; the ten smallest functions share the last tile, $673.6 billion.

table.caption: Net federal outlays by budget function, fiscal 2026

columns.label: Function, as the Treasury names it

source_line: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement, September 2026, Table 9, outlays by function, fiscal 2026, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Tiles show the functions with positive net outlays, $7,566.3 billion against total net outlays of $7,395.8 billion; offsetting receipts and Commerce and Housing Credit, both negative, are left out.
notes_internal: Maker A, round 2. Data plan row 48, rule 14.52. Domain D08. Source line: the sidecar's treemap_fy2026 variant.

Data lead rulings (a) and (e), as RF-1 of the review fix pass changed them: Social Security takes the subject ink through labels.named, its words in the label-on-subject ink, with no keyline and no plate; every other tile takes the track ink with a 1 px edge in the context ink (Rule 05.1: an area form spends no red).

Every figure checked by script (fixfigs.py, scratch, fix pass): 17 positive functions summing to 7,566.3 billion; Social Security the largest, 1,667.1, 22 percent of them; the ten functions under Veterans' benefits and services, each under 2 percent (Transportation 1.89 the largest), folding to 673.6 billion, 8.9 percent.

labels.fold 'fit' folds the fewest smallest functions that let every tile hold its words at 256 px (entry 14.52's test, RF-10): ten, so Veterans' benefits and services, 5.5 percent, keeps its tile; the fold tile is laid out last, at the bottom right at every width. The phone heights grew to hold Veterans' words (716 px at 358, 651 at 296, 666 at 256).
